title: Piano style with Kelly and Petit; trumpet leads the band off
summary: He describes vamp-style piano with both hands and how the trumpet player knocked off the band with two bass-drum beats before each number.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Okay, we were asking about the style of piano you played for instance with Chris Kelly or Buddy Petit. Yeah. If you'd use that vamp style of both hands going one on the first and the second piano.

Yeah, that's right. Just like that. That's right. Just like that. That's one time. Then sometimes you… Sometimes both hands together. Both hands, yeah. Both hands, yeah. Four, four times, according to calling. That's right. And at that time when you're playing drum most of the trumpet players, see everything was built around the trumpet at that time, you know what I mean? And most everything you played the trumpet, two licks on your bass drum, boom boom, then they started. That's right.
But that two on your bass drum, you mean the drummer would give that to someone?

Yeah, yeah. He'd give that to, I mean like you said you're going to play Panama Ray, all right. And he'd say, you know the panel record, da da da da da da da da da. Well before he started panel records he'd say, the drummer started off, boom boom, then the trumpet, da da da da da da da da da. Boom boom, da da da da da da da da. Boom boom, da da da da da da da. That's what I mean.
I thought many of you would stomp in places stomping off, giving you two beats of the bass
No, no, no, no. To reach over and hit on the bass drum or something. I wasn't sure.
The trumpet player would always knock the band off. He'd give you two licks with his feet like that and he'd knock the band off and then you'd pick up.
Did the trumpet player ever stop playing hardly during a number? Or did he keep going all the time?
